  <div class="about-copy">
    <p>I am an economic historian studying why wealth and opportunity are so unevenly shared, and why some people and countries recover from hard times more easily than others. My research focuses mainly on Africa.</p>
    <p>I use historical records about people, families, and communities to understand how changes in the economy affect everyday life. Who owns land and other valuable resources, who can borrow money, and who has political power can shape who gets through a crisis and who falls further behind. My work follows these differences across generations and helps explain why the gains from economic growth are often unevenly shared.</p>
    <p>I hold an MSc and PhD in Economic History from Lund University and have worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Lund and the University of Cambridge. My work contributes to research projects supported by the Swedish Research Council, Riksbankens Jubileumsfond, Handelsbanken Research Foundations, and the UK Arts and Humanities Research Council. I have also carried out research and consultancy for STINT and the United Nations Development Programme.</p>
